differences.what: massing: the draft's generic block is now the photograph's: a light stone front two storeys over a raised basement, its corona at about 11.7 m and the mansard's curb near 15.7 m; the front's north corner, the cornice along it and both street dormers lie within about 10-15 px of the print's

the canted bay at the front's south end, carried through both storeys and up through the cornice under its own slated crown with a cresting, a light in each face on each storey at the front's heights, where the print has it (x 470-690 px)

the porch on columns at the stoop's head, its entablature about 5.7-6.35 m and a balcony on it before the window over the door; the terrace along the front at the principal floor north of the stoop; the broad stoop
three opening columns north of the bay (the door's and two windows'), the chamber windows over the principal ones, each window under a hood
the deep cornice on paired brackets over a frieze, turned round the bay and along the south flank
the slated mansard with two dormers on its street face (over the door's column and between the two northern columns) and one on its south face
a low coped stone wall before the lawn, broken by the walk before the stoop, in place of the draft's fence

every street window in the print is ROUND-HEADED under a moulded hood with a carved crown; the build cuts square-headed sash under K09's cornice hood. A K01 stone front lays round arches only as street_front_openings (1612's), which this piece did not take on — T-3208
the window over the porch is a PAIRED, arched window (two lights under one head, about 1.25 m wide); the build stands one sash of the front's width there — T-3208

the south flank's front part is the same light STONE as the front in the print; the build lays it in K03 brick, because the 1911 sheet records 'brick with stone front' and K01 returns stone along a flank only with a quoined corner the print does not show — T-3208 to weigh with the later pictures
the dormers' heads are ARCHED under projecting hoods on consoles; built as K05's gabled head — T-3208
the bay's crown carries a DORMER on its front face (the print's x 600-680 px, and the mid-century and 2024 fronts); K08's mansard crown takes none — T-3208
the porch's columns are a pair a side with responds and the balcony's rail stands about 0.5 m higher than built (0.35 m, the most K01's hood leaves under the window's sill) — T-3208
the terrace stands on carved brackets over the basement with its basement lights between them, and a low rail on it; built as a solid stone terrace — T-3208
the square stone posts at the walk's opening and at the lot's front corners, and the stoop's stone posts at its foot — T-3208
the bay's crown reads a little higher and broader in the print, whose top edge cuts it at about 15.3 m; built 4.0 m over its eaves

the corona over the bay reads about 1 m higher in the print than in the render at the bay's south cheek (y 181 against about 240 px), where the camera's fit and the 1911 sheet's bay disagree (the sheet bulges 1.8 m at v 2.0-6.1, the print 0.93 m at v 0.3-4.3); the print's reading is built; the residual is over the bar, so either the bay's cornice or the camera's fit at its corner is to be reworked by T-3208 against the later fronts
colour and the stone's tone: the print is monochrome sepia
the north flank, the rear and the sheet's frame range behind: the print does not see them; the south flank's canted bay stands behind the neighbour at the print's left

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153). A ticket whose ## Image gate names this building does not close while it is not "matches" (tools/image_gate.mjs).
